title: Agentic Expansion of the Domain Knowledge Repository Concept
text: Medium Agentic Expansion of the Domain Knowledge Repository Concept | by Michael Zummo | Oct, 2026 | Medium Sitemap Open in app Sign up Sign in Medium Logo Get app Write Search Sign up Sign in Press enter or click to view image in full size AI Knowledge Management Product Management User Experience Agentic Ai Agentic Expansion of the Domain Knowledge Repository Concept Michael Zummo 2 min read · Oct 9, 2026 -- Listen Share My role recently stepped deeper into AI. As I dug into agentic development I began noticing similarities with how humans understand and perform roles. Something woke me up this morning that I just had to share. From the moment my eyes opened, I realized a downward expansion of the Domain Knowledge Repository model — “Skills.” Press enter or click to view image in full size It certainly made sense for humans and could help inform learning and development groups or curriculum. But it was the parallel image in my mind that rocked me. Press enter or click to view image in full size There is a parallel model for agentic solutions. If we further push the skills tier to something useful for shaping development we get something like… Press enter or click to view image in full size Workflow steps could come from journey maps, service design blueprints, BA swim lanes / process maps, JTBD, etc. Then we map which specific skills would be used as rows and high-level details about the aspect leveraged in each intersecting cell as appropriate. A similar skill map could be shaped for human learning and development. Before Agentic Skill Mapping Let me take one tiny step backwards. Before doing that agentic skill mapping we should first evaluate which actors would optimize a workflow. There are three options: human, automation, and agent. Press enter or click to view image in full size For anything that is an agent then we can determine what skills are required for that agent in that workflow step. This feels like a very logical and useful expansion of the DKR concept with a practical onramp.
